Getting started with simregdata

Source: vignettes/simregdata.Rmd
simregdata.Rmd

simregdata returns simulated CBS microdata through a drop-in read_sav(). Code written against it runs unchanged in CBS Remote Access, where the same call reads the real file.

Read a file 

library(haven)
library(simregdata)  # after haven, so read_sav() is the simulator's

sim_init("woonbase", year = 2023, n = 5000, seed = 42)

pers <- read_sav("WoonbasePopulatiePersonen2023V1",
                 col_select = c(RINPERSOON, HUISHOUDNR1Jan, TYPHH1Jan))
head(pers)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 3
#>   RINPERSOON HUISHOUDNR1Jan TYPHH1Jan                    
#>   <chr>      <chr>          <int+lbl>                    
#> 1 488404786  000000000001   8 [Institutioneel huishouden]
#> 2 371027360  000000000001   8 [Institutioneel huishouden]
#> 3 639972388  000000000001   8 [Institutioneel huishouden]
#> 4 656756076  000000000001   8 [Institutioneel huishouden]
#> 5 181341029  000000000001   8 [Institutioneel huishouden]
#> 6 834905395  000000000001   8 [Institutioneel huishouden]

sim_init() builds a shared population spine of persons, households and dwellings; every dataset draws from it. sim_catalog() lists all file names.

Labels and codes

Categorical columns are haven::labelled, as in real .sav files. cbs_code() recovers the original CBS character codes:

table(as_factor(pers$TYPHH1Jan))
#> 
#>            Eenpersoonshuishouden Niet-gehuwd paar zonder kinderen 
#>                              783                              316 
#>      Gehuwd paar zonder kinderen    Niet-gehuwd paar met kinderen 
#>                              874                              374 
#>         Gehuwd paar met kinderen               Eenouderhuishouden 
#>                             1334                              365 
#>                Overig huishouden        Institutioneel huishouden 
#>                               26                              412 
#>             Meerdere huishoudens 
#>                                0

sim_init("rdw", year = 2023)
rdw <- read_sav("RDWNPACT2023TABV1", n_max = 5)
cbs_code(rdw$BRANDSTCODECORVRTG)
#> [1] "1" "1" "1" "1" "2"

Joins across files

Identifiers (RINPERSOON, HUISHOUDNR, RINOBJECTNUMMER, RINPERSOONHKW) come from the spine, so joins between datasets match as on the real data:

sim_init("inpatab", year = 2023)
inpa <- read_sav("INPA2023TABV1", col_select = c(RINPERSOON, INPPERSBESTINK))

joined <- merge(pers, inpa, by = "RINPERSOON")
nrow(joined) / nrow(pers)
#> [1] 1

Export to parquet

For larger runs, sim_population() writes a sample of the population to parquet in the CBS folder layout; sim_set_data_root() then makes read_sav() read those files instead of simulating:

sim_population("sim_data", datasets = c("woonbase", "rdw"),
               years = 2019:2023, fraction = 0.01)
sim_set_data_root("sim_data")

sim_scan_columns() finds the col_select columns your scripts use, so the export only writes what you need.

Other files

read_sav() passes any name it does not recognise to haven::read_sav(), so one call works for simulated and real files. Datasets of your own can be added from a YAML file with sim_create_custom() and sim_register().

How it works

Each dataset is defined in YAML under inst/config/datasets/: a manifest, codelists, column definitions and year-specific parameters. The parameters are calibrated to CBS StatLine and stored in the package, so generating data needs no network. The *_update_params() functions refresh them.

Persons have a deterministic life course (birth, death, migration), so the population changes between years while identifiers stay stable. Building the spine for one million persons takes about 10 seconds.

Results on simulated data are for checking code, not for interpretation. The worked examples, starting with vignette("quality-cars"), show which results look like the published statistics and what changes in Remote Access. See the provenance article for where each parameter comes from.
